title: Siegard graph
description: The derived index of a knowledge root. Never authored and never edited: `bin/graph.py` derives it from the markdown nodes, and `--check` holds a committed copy to them. Nodes are the files; edges are the references their frontmatter declares. A relationship stated only in prose is not an edge, because two readings of one paragraph produce two graphs.

file.description: The node's file, relative to the knowledge root. Always `<id>.md`.

digest.description: Content identity: the SHA-256 of this node's file, computable by hand as `sha256sum <knowledge-root>/<id>.md`. A task's binding carries the digest of each node it read, and this is where it reads them from — so what a binding pinned is the node's own bytes, not the shape of the index around it. Whole file, frontmatter and body: a digest over the frontmatter alone would miss what `## Rules` points at and could not be recomputed with one command.

gaps.description: The fields this node declares absent, by gap `field` name, sorted. Omitted when none. The `why` behind each stays in the node file.

at.description: Where in the source node the reference sits, so a reader can open the place a defect names.
